name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: We should adopt a 4.5:1 contrast focus ring at 4px width with 3px offset on every interactive element. This provides sufficient visual clarity for users with visual impairments, while also being subtle enough not to overwhelm other design elements. By choosing this option, we're accepting a trade-off between aesthetics and accessibility, as a thicker or more prominent focus ring might be more noticeable but could also disrupt the overall visual flow. This decision ensures that users who rely on keyboard navigation can clearly see where they are on the page, which is essential for making EXCAVA usable by everyone.

name: Reader
text: A 4px ring at 4.5:1 contrast risks blending into low-contrast UI or appearing bulky on mobile touch targets. A 3px ring at 3:1 contrast is more reliable across devices but may disappear on patterned backgrounds. Test both on actual EXCAVA screens with real users to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt the 3px focus ring at 3:1 contrast. It survives low-contrast backgrounds and stays crisp on mobile touch targets without bulking up. The trade-off is that it’s slightly harder to spot at a glance, but that’s better than losing it entirely on patterned screens. Real users will notice the difference more than designers.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-2869, worker-5357 — done, dissolved]

name: Reader
text: A 3px ring at 3:1 contrast vanishes for users with moderate low vision or in bright ambient light—it’s not just “slightly harder,” it’s often invisible. Test a 4px ring at 4.5:1 on high-contrast and low-contrast backgrounds with real screen-reader users; if it fails on patterned screens, add a 1px inner shadow at 7:1 to cut through patterns without bulk.
